description: During the 2026-08-07 bookkeeping pass, scripts/gen_api_docs.py silently ran 'cargo install rustdoc-md --locked' when it found the binary missing. The CLAUDE.md bookkeeping-pass routine says to REPORT a missing tool and note it in the hand-off, not to install it -- an agent told not to install anything cannot comply if the script installs on its behalf. title: scripts/gen_api_docs.py auto-installs rustdoc-md without asking

description:
Mirrors GitHub issue #26 ("Tampines Steam Tables Plotter and GUI"). Build an
eframe/egui GUI, as a new example binary under tampines-steam-tables
(examples/steam_table_plotter/, following the fhr_sim_v1 /
transient_rankine_cycle / depressurisation convention -- egui/eframe/
egui_plot/egui_extras are already dev-dependencies there, target-gated off
Android), for figure generation and interactive inspection -- NOT a full
simulator.

MAINTAINER DIRECTION (2026-08-20, beyond the GH issue): FOUR interactive
tabs, not three -- T-p, p-h, T-s, AND h-s (the issue listed p-h/h-s as
required and T-s as optional; the maintainer wants all four, T-p included).
Every tab must support CSV export (for external plotting) and PNG/PDF export.

Required per tab, from issue #26:
  - Saturation dome, sat-liquid/sat-vapour lines
  - Quality lines x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 (Region 4 lever rule:
    x = (h - hf(p)) / (hg(p) - hf(p)) -- NOT independently validated data,
    say so if presented)
  - Selected isobars / isotherms where applicable
  - Region-boundary / critical-point / triple-point markers
  - Overlay layers for real validation/reference data, toggleable, DISABLED
    (not fabricated) if the dataset isn't available for that diagram:
      - Moody critical-flow states: crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/tests/moody_critical_mass_flux_homogeneous_eqm.rs
      - Zaloudek/Saha critical-flow states: .../tests/zaloudek_mass_flux_hom_eqm/*.rs
      - Marviken blowdown: .../tests/marviken_tests.rs
      - Edwards-O'Brien blowdown trajectory: crates/tampines-steam-tables/tests/edwards_blowdown.rs
      - Wagner/IAPWS property validation points: search
        src/interfaces/tests_and_examples/ and src/interfaces/functional_programming/
        for embedded reference states (ph_flash_region4_edge_and_region5.rs,
        pt_flash_eqm/envelope_corner_tests.rs, ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs, and the
        single_phase_table_*.rs / saturation_table_*.rs fixtures under
        interfaces/tests_and_examples/ph_flash_steam_table/) -- these look
        like exactly the kind of embedded reference states the issue asks to
        export via a small CSV exporter path.
  - All plotted curves computed LIVE from tampines-steam-tables's own routines
    (not hardcoded numbers), so plots stay traceable to the implementation.

Do NOT fabricate any validation point. If a dataset genuinely cannot be
sourced from the crate, disable that layer/checkbox rather than inventing
numbers -- this is a hard requirement from the GH issue, restated here.

Export requirements: PNG (required), PDF (feasible effort, may need a
different render backend than egui_plot's live canvas -- search the
workspace for an existing PDF/plotting dependency before adding a new one,
per the root CLAUDE.md "search the workspace before building anything" hard
rule), CSV for both plotted curves and validation points, SVG optional if
easy. Suggested output directory per the issue: figures/property_validation/.

Conventions: root CLAUDE.md Rust design rules (enum dispatch not trait
objects, no Box<T>, no lifetime parameters, uom at signatures where it
already applies in this crate). Follow the existing fhr_sim_v1 example's
Android-gating pattern (`#![cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]` +
Android stub main + all desktop items cfg-gated) so
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android`
stays clean. V&V doc-comment convention (methodology + results) applies to
any new plotted-vs-reference comparison this GUI displays.

Related/adjacent beads (do not duplicate their scope): op-21g.3 (future move
of GUI examples to a dedicated app crate -- not blocking, still Todo, build
in tampines-steam-tables per current convention and the maintainer's explicit
instruction); op-zfr.4 (keep GUI out of unconditional library builds -- this
work is an example, already satisfies that).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Session 1 survey + design decisions.

SURVEYED (reuse-first rule): all plotted curves can be computed live from public
crate routines -- sat_pressure_4/sat_temp_4 (region 4), h_tp_1/s_tp_1/v_tp_1
(region 1), h_tp_2/s_tp_2/v_tp_2 (region 2), h_rho_t_3/s_rho_t_3 + v_tp_3{c,s,u,y,t,r,x,z}
(region 3, needed above 623.15 K where x_ph_flash switches branch), plus the
functional-programming flashes (t_ph_eqm, s_ph_eqm, x_ph_flash, ph_flash_region).
No new library code needed.

REFERENCE DATA FOUND (all real, all in-repo):
 - Moody 1975 Fig.1: 13 isobars, (h/h_ref, G/G_ref) with p_ref=100 psi,
   h_ref=100 BTU_IT/lbm -> real (p0,h0) stagnation states.
 - Zaloudek: 21 throat-quality curves, (p_throat_psia, G_lbps_ft2, h0_btu_lbm);
   throat states are (p_sat, x_t) Region-4 states -> directly plottable.
 - Marviken NUREG/CR-2671 Fig 8:24: TEST_23_POINTS (29) and TEST_24_POINTS (40),
   (p0_kPa, G); h0 computed live by the same rule the test uses.
 - Edwards-O'Brien B-T-3271: 24-node initial (p=7 MPa, T) profile Table 1, and
   the 16-point digitised GS-1 measured pressure trace.
 - Wagner/Kretzschmar International Steam Tables: 5 saturation tables (371 rows)
   and 29 single-phase isobar tables (2386 rows) under
   src/interfaces/tests_and_examples/ph_flash_steam_table/.

DEPENDENCIES: no new workspace dependency needed. PNG via 'image' and PDF via
'lopdf' -- BOTH already in root [workspace.dependencies] (image for GUI examples,
lopdf for kovan-literature). Adding them to tampines-steam-tables'
[target.'cfg(not(target_os = "android"))'.dev-dependencies] only.

ARCHITECTURE: backend-independent Scene (polylines/markers/text) rendered by an
enum-dispatched backend (Svg | Pdf | Png) so PNG/PDF/SVG are the SAME figure.
Critically, the export path is a pure function independent of egui, so it can be
driven headless -- this container has no display, so the GUI itself can only be
compile-verified; a --headless/--export-all CLI mode makes the export path
actually runnable and testable here.

NEXT: mechanical extraction of the reference data into
examples/steam_table_plotter/reference_data/ with provenance citations (the
fixtures are #[cfg(test)] locals inside test fns, so no exporter can reach them
without hoisting them to consts in ~35 files -- option (a) from the brief).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
SESSION 1 COMPLETE -- all stated goals met, tree compiles clean, nothing committed.

WHAT WAS BUILT
crates/tampines-steam-tables/examples/steam_table_plotter/  (new, ~5.6k lines)
  main.rs            Android stub + CLI (--export-all / --out-dir / --samples / --help)
  app.rs             eframe/egui GUI: 4 tabs, layer checkboxes, axis + resolution
                     controls, per-tab export buttons, on-screen caveat panel
  diagram.rs         DiagramKind enum (T-p, p-h, T-s, h-s) + projection
  data.rs            ThermoPoint (uom-typed p/T/h/s/x) + PlotLayer
  curves.rs          ALL curves computed live from IF97 (dome, quality lines,
                     isobars, isotherms, region boundaries, crit/triple points)
  layers.rs          16-layer registry + the availability table
  export.rs          scene assembly, footnotes, file writing
  figure/            font.rs (stroke font), layout.rs (Scene -> draw ops),
                     svg.rs, pdf.rs, png.rs, csv_export.rs
  reference_data/    moody.rs, zaloudek.rs, marviken.rs, edwards.rs, wagner.rs
  README.md
Cargo.toml: [[example]] entry with test = true; image.workspace = true added to
the android-gated dev-deps; "figures" added to package exclude.
.gitignore: /figures/ (regenerable, tens of MB).

FOUR TABS -- ALL COMPLETE, none partial. Each supports CSV + PNG + PDF (+ SVG).

EXPORT -- all four formats work, verified by running them:
  PNG  via image (workspace dep already); own AA rasteriser
  PDF  written directly, ~80 lines, no dependency at all. VERIFIED with poppler:
       pdfinfo reports 'PDF version 1.4, Pages 1, 720x540 pts', and pdftoppm
       renders it identically to the PNG. lopdf was considered and rejected --
       with the stroke font there are no font/image/annotation objects, so a
       page is one path stream.
  SVG  standalone, no external font reference
  CSV  two per tab (curves / reference points), full state per row incl.
       quality and reference mass flux, provenance on every row, byte-reproducible
Output: crates/tampines-steam-tables/figures/property_validation/ (issue #26's
suggested path, resolved from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR like tests/edwards_blowdown.rs).
20 files per run.

OVERLAY LAYERS -- ALL SEVEN WIRED TO REAL DATA, none left disabled for want of data:
  Wagner/IAPWS saturation table   220 rows
  Wagner/IAPWS single-phase       2334 rows (29 isobar tables)
  Moody 1975 Fig.1                321 stagnation states across 13 isobars
  Zaloudek                        357 throat states across 21 quality curves
  Marviken NUREG/CR-2671          29 + 40 (test 23 + test 24)
  Edwards-O'Brien initial states  24 measured node (p,T)
  Edwards-O'Brien GS-1 trace      16 measured pressures -- T-p TAB ONLY
The GS-1 trace is the one deliberate restriction: only pressure was measured, so
it is disabled on p-h / T-s / h-s with a stated reason rather than given an
invented enthalpy. 10 of 64 layer-diagram pairs are disabled -- 3 for missing
data (GS-1), 7 for degeneracy (quality lines + both saturation branch lines on
T-p, isobars on T-p/p-h, isotherms on T-p/T-s) -- each with a reason string shown
in the UI, and the count is pinned by a test.

V&V -- 25 example tests, all pass. The load-bearing gate is
curves::saturation_curve_matches_the_wagner_steam_table: the plotted dome vs all
220 published Wagner rows, 0.5 %% on p_sat and max(0.5 %%, 1 kJ/kg) on h_f/h_g,
209 rows checked, 0 degC to within 1 K of T_c. PASSES 2026-08-20.

CHECKS RUN (all clean)
  cargo build -p tampines-steam-tables --example steam_table_plotter --release  0 warnings
  cargo test  --release -p tampines-steam-tables --example steam_table_plotter  25 passed
  cargo test  --release -p tampines-steam-tables --lib                          959 passed, 13 ignored
  cargo check --workspace --lib --tests                                          clean
  cargo clippy -p tampines-steam-tables --example steam_table_plotter --release  0 findings in the example
  cargo check -p tampines-steam-tables --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android  CLEAN
    (I installed the aarch64-linux-android target; --all-targets, so the example
     is covered, not just --lib)
  rustfmt applied to all new files

TWO LIBRARY DEFECTS FOUND, filed, NOT fixed (out of scope, worked around in the
plotter only):
  op-hidb (P1) x_ph_flash Region-3 saturated-liquid sub-region chain picks
               v_tp_3y below p_crit. At T_sat=646.503 K it returns
               h_f = -1.108e21 kJ/kg -- FINITE, so is_finite() passes it. This
               actually broke the first p-h figure (whole enthalpy axis went to
               -1.1e21). Affects x_ph_flash itself, hence kappa_t_ph_eqm and the
               choked-flow dispatcher, in that ~0.6 K band.
  op-l1tz (P2) region_fwd_eqn_single_phase classifies near-critical compressed
               liquid as Region 2. Not quantified.

NOT DONE / OPEN
  - README math not machine-validated: neither pandoc nor cmark-gfm is installed
    in this container. Checked by eye against the CLAUDE.md conservative subset
    (\frac only, explicit braces, no cases/matrix/boxed, no Unicode Greek).
  - GUI never run interactively: this container has no display. Everything the
    GUI reads is covered by tests (incl. a per-tab finite-plottable-data gate),
    and the whole export path runs headless, but the egui widget layer itself is
    compile-verified only. Worth one human run before sign-off.
  - No version bump, no changelog entry (never-auto-bump rule).

STATUS: leaving in_progress rather than closing -- per the task brief, closing is
the maintainer's call. Nothing is known outstanding on the issue-#26 scope.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
UPDATE 2026-08-21, commit 7634ae96. Addressed the two outstanding items from
the GitHub thread since the rename/theming/custom-lines/file-browser round
(5e00e0e0) and the hover-coordinates request (already in that same commit,
turned out to need no further work):

1. Wagner/Kretzschmar data promoted from a GUI-local ~3,100-line duplicate to
   a first-class library type, tampines_steam_tables::tabulated_data::
   TabulatedData -- ::isobar/::isotherm (tolerance-based cross-sections of
   the published single-phase table) and ::saturation_curve, plus
   TabulatedQuantity to dispatch by enum. Wired into the plotter: the
   built-in Isobars/Isotherms layers now pair each computed IAPWS-IF97 line
   with the matching published Wagner rows as crosses, on every diagram --
   exactly "plot the tabulated data as crosses and iapws97 data as lines".
   A value the crate's default sweep includes but Wagner never tabulated
   correctly shows no crosses (5 bar), not fabricated ones.
2. Custom quality lines -- CustomLineType gained a sixth variant, Quality,
   through the same slider/CSV mechanism the other five already use.

Caught a real bug along the way: a naive ThermodynamicTemperature-typed
tolerance for the isotherm query matched ZERO rows, because uom's
ThermodynamicTemperature does affine (absolute-scale) unit conversion --
converting a "0.5 K window" via .get::<degree_celsius>() gives -272.65, not
0.5. Fixed by taking the tolerance as a plain f64 delta; documented the trap
for the next person reaching for this pattern.

Tests: 5 new library tests, 1 new GUI test (isobar/isotherm crosses pairing,
including the "no match is correct" case). tampines-steam-tables lib 964
passed/0 failed/13 ignored (unchanged ignore count); GUI example 33 passed/0
failed; workspace check clean.

Leaving this in_progress, not closing -- issue #26 is still open on GitHub
and may accumulate further requests (it has been iterative). Update the
GitHub issue and close when the maintainer confirms it's done.

description:
From the op-ffg6 audit, 2026-08-13. API-breaking but NO downstream consumers, so the break is internal-only. ~3 days. Depends on C1. Big mechanical diff, low judgement content -- good candidate to parallelise across agents.

  heat_transfer_correlations/nusselt_number_correlations/pipe_correlations.rs -- 95 panic!, all in pub fn ... -> f64.
    These are CORRELATION validity-range violations, not property-table range errors:
    'gnielinski Re > 1e6, too high', 'Sieder Tate Pr < 0.7, too low'. Needs C1's CorrelationRangeError variant --
    ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError is the wrong name for these and reusing it would be misleading.
  fluid_mechanics_correlations/dimensionalisation.rs -- 20 panic!, same shape. Nonphysical input (viscosity <= 0,
    density <= 0, hydraulic diameter <= 0). Needs C1's NonPhysicalInput variant.

None of these names appears in any downstream crate, so despite being signature changes on public functions the blast
radius is confined to this crate.

description:
Maintainer report, 2026-08-13 07:2x (filed outside active hours; NOT yet reproduced or diagnosed -- mechanism below is the maintainer's description plus an inference, not a verified root cause).

REPORTED: htgr_sim_v1 keeps crashing at LOW temperatures. Maintainer wants the new steel properties (op-x0v1 / op-v9u5) to be usable inside htgr_sim_v1, and expects that to fix this.

INFERRED mechanism to CHECK FIRST (do not assume it):
- The steel/solid property correlations currently in use likely panic or return NaN below some lower validity bound, and the sim hits it at cold start / ambient initial conditions / a cooldown transient.
- So the requirement is a validity range that spans BOTH ends: ambient (~20-25 degC) up through 1200 degC. op-x0v1 was written up as a high-temperature ask; this report shows the LOW end is what is actually breaking today.

DIAGNOSIS STEPS (active hours):
1. Reproduce -- run htgr_sim_v1 and capture the actual panic message + backtrace. Do not fix from the inference above.
2. Identify which correlation and which crate it lives in (tuas SolidMaterial / offbeat material library / tampines / foam thermophysics).
3. Record the correlation's ACTUAL stated validity range and the temperature the sim reached.

FIX CONSTRAINT -- do not silently widen the physics:
- Extrapolating a correlation outside its published validity range, or clamping without saying so, fabricates property values. That is not an acceptable fix on its own.
- Acceptable: (a) source data that genuinely covers the low end and extend the range with the citation; (b) clamp at the validity bound AND surface it (documented in the doc comment, and visible/logged at runtime rather than silent); (c) fix the sim so it does not enter that state if the state is itself unphysical.
- Whichever is chosen, the doc comment must state the real validity range and what happens outside it.

Related: op-x0v1 (1200 C steel properties), op-v9u5 (OSTI + NIST source ingestion -- check whether either source covers the low-temperature end).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
CORRECTION + REAL EVIDENCE from maintainer, 2026-08-13 07:2x. Supersedes the 'low temperature / ambient / cold start' inference in the original description -- that was WRONG.

ACTUAL FAILURE:
  htgr-physics failed in helium primary loop (circulator + hot gas duct)
  (crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95:81):
  called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError

'Low temp' in the maintainer's phrasing means ~700+ degC -- i.e. LOW relative to the HTGR envelope, but it is the correlation's UPPER validity bound that is being exceeded. The solid material's range tops out around 700 degC and the hot gas duct / circulator solid nodes run past it.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS HERE -- fix both, do not conflate:

(1) RANGE TOO NARROW (the physics fix, = op-x0v1).
    The steel correlation in use tops out near 700 degC. HTGR hot-leg helium is ~750-950 degC depending on the plant, so the range is simply unfit for this application. Needs sourced properties to 1200 degC. Confirm the exact current bound and which SolidMaterial variant is selected for the hot gas duct.

(2) UNWRAP ON A RECOVERABLE ERROR (the robustness fix, TUAS).
    calculation.rs:95 `.unwrap()`s a Result whose Err variant is a normal, anticipatable out-of-range condition. That converts a diagnosable property-range error into a panic that takes down the whole sim and reports no temperature, no node, and no material. Propagate the error (or at minimum surface WHICH material, WHICH node, and WHAT temperature was requested vs the allowed range) instead of unwrapping.
    This is worth fixing even after the range is widened -- the next material to go out of range should produce a usable message, not a bare panic.

Check whether the same unwrap pattern appears elsewhere in one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/ and its fluid-array siblings.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, 2026-08-13 07:3x (read from source; panic not re-run -- htgr_sim_v1 is an egui GUI example with no headless mode yet, see op-szmi.3).

THE NUMBER: SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L is tabulated to a MAX of 1000 K = 726.85 degC.
  crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/solid_database/ss_304_l.rs:705-712
    max_temp_ss_304l_zou_zweibaum_spline() -> 1000 K
    min_temp_ss_304l_zou_zweibaum_spline() ->  250 K
  Bounds are enforced by range_check() in .../boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/mod.rs:239, which returns
  TuasLibError::ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError. That is the Err that gets unwrapped.

WHY IT BITES htgr_sim_v1 SO EASILY -- the margin is 27 K:
  HTR-10 phase-1 published core outlet = 700 degC = 973.15 K
    (crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/design.rs:118, helium_outlet_phase1)
  SS304L ceiling                       = 726.85 degC = 1000 K
  => ~26.85 K of headroom at the NOMINAL design point. Any transient overshoot exits the range.
  HTR-10 phase 2 (900 degC outlet) would be ~173 K OUTSIDE the range and cannot be modelled at all today.

THE PANICKING CALL SITE:
  one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95
    .map(|&temperature| try_get_rho_cp(material, temperature, pressure).unwrap())
  Inside a closure in an iterator chain, which is why it is an unwrap and not a  -- fixing it means
  collecting into Result<Array1<_>, _> (collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?) rather than just swapping the operator.
  The reported column is :95:81, which matches the .unwrap() on that line.

THE CONSUMER: the steam generator's tube metal is SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L
  (examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/primary_loop.rs:481, in steam_generator_config()).
  The 'circulator + hot gas duct' label is the stage marker at physics/mod.rs:313; the primary step owns
  the steam generator, so the failing SolidColumn is the SG TUBE METAL, not a duct wall.

THIS CEILING IS ALREADY A KNOWN, DOCUMENTED CONSTRAINT -- the code works around it rather than fixing it:
  - physics/mod.rs:556-577 -- the whole-plant smoke test asserts metal stays below 1000 K, and records that a
    50% rod bank insertion 'dies at 6 s when the tube metal passes SteelSS304L's 1000 K ceiling and TUAS panics'.
  - physics/primary_loop.rs:1286-1330 -- core_inlet_responds_to_secondary_heat_removal deliberately throttles to
    2.2 kg/s instead of 1.0 kg/s BECAUSE 1.0 kg/s 'drives the tube metal through the steel limit and kills the run'.
  So a test was weakened to stay inside this range. Widening the range should let that test go back to 1.0 kg/s --
  check that when the properties land.

SECOND CEILING NEARBY (do not lose it): IF97 stops at 1073.15 K, per the same docs. Widening the steel range
alone will not make an excursion survivable; it moves the failure to the steam side. Note it, do not fix it here.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: TYPO REPAIR for the note above: line reading "which is why it is an unwrap and not a  -- fixing it means" should read "which is why it is an unwrap and not a question-mark operator". A shell backtick ate the character. No other content affected.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
DUPLICATE (partial) — overlaps the pre-existing op-szmi.17 (P1, 2026-08-12): 'SolidColumn steel property tables panic above 1000 K — the SG kills the sim too easily'. Filed by me 2026-08-13 without first searching the store.

op-szmi.17 is the better bead on the PHYSICS side: it frames the 1000 K limit as a property-table limit rather than a material limit, proposes a three-part fix (guard the call site with a pause-and-explain modal, extend/replace the property data, feed metal temperature to the RPS), and records the interaction with the reactor protection system being disarmed by default.

What op-m1jz adds that op-szmi.17 does NOT have, and which is worth keeping:
  - the exact panicking call site, one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95, and the fact that it is an .unwrap() inside an iterator closure (so the fix needs collect::<Result<_,_>>(), not a question-mark operator)
  - the exact numbers: max_temp_ss_304l_zou_zweibaum_spline() = 1000 K, min = 250 K, ss_304_l.rs:705-712
  - the ~27 K nominal headroom against HTR-10's published 700 degC core outlet, and that phase 2 (900 degC) is unmodellable today
  - the observation that a test was already weakened to stay in range (primary_loop.rs core_inlet_responds_to_secondary_heat_removal throttles to 2.2 kg/s instead of 1.0 kg/s)

Recommend the maintainer FOLD these details into op-szmi.17 and close this one, rather than keeping two. Not doing it unilaterally.

Also note op-szmi.17 records that property libraries in this workspace panic rather than return Result at roughly 40 sites — that is the same finding op-ffg6 is auditing.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
RESOLVED 2026-08-13 and closing as a DUPLICATE of op-szmi.17, which predates it and covers the same defect.
The crash itself is fixed and pushed: the SG's tube metal now uses SteelSS304LHighTemp (300-1700 K) instead of
SteelSS304L (250-1000 K), so the ~27 K of headroom above HTR-10's published 700 degC core outlet is now ~700 K.
Commits f565d31b (material) and 3acc9536 (wired).
The diagnostic detail this bead added, which op-szmi.17 lacked, has been copied onto that bead: the exact call site
(one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95, an .unwrap() inside an iterator closure), the exact
bounds (ss_304_l.rs:705-712), the 27 K nominal margin, and the fact that a test had already been weakened to stay
in range.
NOT everything here is done -- the unwrap at calculation.rs:95 is still an unwrap. That half is op-ffg6.2, where it
is a free non-breaking fix because advance_timestep already returns Result.
